Comment: Lack of recognition of adverse effects, flooding, etc.
Response: See final statement, page 5 et seq.
Comment: Partial relevance to rural housing.
Response: Housing technology is transferable to rural housing applications. Planning concerns groups of housing, wherever located.
Comment: Implications of new materials.
Response: See final statement, page 5 and 6. Questions of durability are incorporated in the Guide Criteria.
Comment: Special housing requirements of Mexican-Americans.
Response: Discussion of this and other "Type B" BREAKTHROUGH research projects has been deleted from this statement as inappropriate to its purpose. The study in question was undertaken in response to one specific proposal received in that part of the BREAKTHROUGH competition.
Comment: Wild cherry trees at Kalamazoo.
Response: These trees are being retained as part of the landscape design, with appropriate protection for grade changes.
Comment: Storm water handling.
Response: See final statement, pages 8, 11 and 12.
C. Department of the Interior
Comment: Develop details for each site.
Response: See final statement, which addresses program elements in considerably more detail than was done in the draft statement. Some of the tabular information has been included in the Appendices.
Comment: Site conditions and amenities.
Response: See final statement for range of planning considerations for each site. Note specifically that BREAKTHROUGH communities are designed for a range of income and other characteristics, rather than to cater to specific groups as noted in the comment.
<u>Comment</u>: Problems of psychological reaction to too close living.
Response: "Massive multiste housing" has been used only in central city sites for smaller family units, as discussed in the text.
